summary: Over forty days the risen Jesus opens the Scriptures to His disciples, names them His witnesses, and tells them to wait in Jerusalem for the promised Spirit.
key_insight: Jesus said forgiveness was to be preached to all nations “beginning at Jerusalem,” the city whose crowds had just shouted for His death. The first offer of pardon in His name would go to the place that crucified Him.
story: For forty days after His suffering, Jesus presented Himself alive to the apostles “by many infallible proofs,” appearing to them and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God.

He told them, “These are the words which I spoke to you while I was still with you, that all things must be fulfilled which were written in the Law of Moses and the Prophets and the Psalms concerning Me.” Then He opened their understanding, that they might comprehend the Scriptures.

“Thus it is written,” He said, “and thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead the third day, and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. And you are witnesses of these things.”

Gathered with them, He commanded them not to leave Jerusalem but to wait for the Promise of the Father, “which,” He said, “you have heard from Me; for John truly baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days from now.” They were to tarry in the city of Jerusalem until they were endued with power from on high.

When they had come together, they asked Him, “Lord, will You at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?” He answered, “It is not for you to know times or seasons which the Father has put in His own authority. But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”

scene.label: Forty days
scene.text: Only Acts tells how long the risen Jesus stayed with His disciples. The Day of Pentecost, the Feast of Weeks, came about ten days after He was taken up (Acts 2:1), so the wait Jesus spoke of was short.

scene.label: Law, Prophets and Psalms
scene.text: Jews divided their Scriptures into three parts: the Law, the Prophets and the Writings. The Psalms were the largest and best-known book of the Writings. Jesus says every part speaks of Him.

scene.label: The Promise of the Father
scene.text: God had promised through the prophets, “I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh” (Joel 2:28) and “I will put My Spirit within you” (Ezekiel 36:27). On the night before He died, Jesus told the disciples the Father would give them “another Helper” (John 14:16).

scene.label: The kingdom question
scene.text: Many Jews expected the Messiah to restore David’s kingdom to Israel. Jesus does not mock the question; He says the timing belongs to the Father and gives them a task for now. Christians differ on whether His answer leaves room for a future restoration of national Israel or points to the kingdom spreading among the nations.

scene.label: Jerusalem to the ends of the earth
scene.text: Acts 1:8 maps the book of Acts: the church in Jerusalem (chapters 1–7), the gospel in Judea and Samaria (8–12), and then outward through the Gentile world until Paul preaches in Rome (13–28).

witnesses.luke: Luke records these instructions twice, at the end of his Gospel and at the start of Acts, so they join his two volumes. His Gospel draws the teaching together without marking the passing days; Acts supplies the forty days and shows the promise fulfilled. Acts opens by calling the Gospel an account of what Jesus “began both to do and teach” (Acts 1:1); His work continues through His witnesses.

seeing.reveals: Jesus is the subject of the whole Old Testament; His suffering and rising were written there before they happened. He is also Lord of the mission, who sets its message, its starting point and its power.
seeing.living: The disciples asked when; Jesus told them what and how. He gives His people a task rather than a timetable, and He does not send them out on their own strength. Wait on the Spirit He promised, and bear witness to Him where you already live.
seeing.ponder: Are you more eager to know God’s timing than to be Christ’s witness, and are you relying on His power or on your own?

preaching.big_idea: The risen Christ sends witnesses with a message from Scripture and power from the Spirit.
outline: The message: suffering, rising and forgiveness (46–47)
The power: the Promise of the Father (49)
preaching.watch_for: Luke 24:49 and Acts 1:4–8 form a hinge between Luke’s two books. The Gospel closes with the command to wait for power; Acts reopens with the same promise and then shows it given at Pentecost. Read them together.
